cards.front: Complete the guidance about renewal and online procedures, beginning with “The renewal section describes a license lasting five years”.
cards.back: The renewal section describes a license lasting five years and expiring on the holder’s birthday, except that a holder turning twenty-one has an expiration thirty days after that birthday.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about renewal and online procedures, beginning with “Renewal is available up to one hundred eighty days”.
cards.back: Renewal is available up to one hundred eighty days before expiration unless the holder will be turning twenty-one.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about renewal and online procedures, beginning with “Renewing a South Dakota driver”.
cards.back: Renewing a South Dakota driver license requires a vision test.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about renewal and online procedures, beginning with “When the license surrendered for renewal has expired, a”.
cards.back: When the license surrendered for renewal has expired, a knowledge test is required in addition to the vision test.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about renewal and online procedures, beginning with “A foreign-country driver’s license duration is limited to the”.
cards.back: A foreign-country driver’s license duration is limited to the authorized stay documented by USCIS and cannot exceed five years.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about renewal and online procedures, beginning with “The handbook says eligible people may use mail or”.
cards.back: The handbook says eligible people may use mail or online service for replacement and renewal once during any ten-year period.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about renewal and online procedures, beginning with “The handbook states that online processing for license renewals,”.
cards.back: The handbook states that online processing for license renewals, duplicates and restricted-minor-permit upgrades became available July one, two thousand fourteen.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about renewal and online procedures, beginning with “The handbook says a person may apply”.
cards.back: The handbook says a person may apply online to reinstate driving privileges after suspension.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about grounds for license loss, beginning with “A drug conviction involving a vehicle can be”.
cards.back: A drug conviction involving a vehicle can be grounds for losing a South Dakota driver license.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about grounds for license loss, beginning with “A conviction for driving while intoxicated”.
cards.back: A conviction for driving while intoxicated can cause loss of the driver license.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about grounds for license loss, beginning with “An alcohol conviction involving a minor”.
cards.back: An alcohol conviction involving a minor can lead to loss of driving privileges.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about grounds for license loss, beginning with “Refusing an alcohol or drug test requested by”.
cards.back: Refusing an alcohol or drug test requested by a police officer can lead to license loss.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about grounds for license loss, beginning with “Driving during a court-ordered prohibition on”.
cards.back: Driving during a court-ordered prohibition on driving can lead to license loss.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about grounds for license loss, beginning with “Driving while a license is suspended, cancelled, revoked or”.
cards.back: Driving while a license is suspended, cancelled, revoked or denied is a listed reason for losing driving privileges.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about grounds for license loss, beginning with “Providing false information in a driver-license”.
cards.back: Providing false information in a driver-license or non-driver-identification application can cause license loss.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about grounds for license loss, beginning with “Leaving a financial judgment for motor-vehicle-crash damages”.
cards.back: Leaving a financial judgment for motor-vehicle-crash damages unsettled can be grounds for license loss.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about grounds for license loss, beginning with “Attempting to change license information improperly or using another”.
cards.back: Attempting to change license information improperly or using another person’s license is a listed ground for license loss.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about grounds for license loss, beginning with “Failing to attend a reexamination requested”.
cards.back: Failing to attend a reexamination requested by Driver Licensing can cause license loss.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about grounds for license loss, beginning with “Using a motor vehicle to commit a felony or”.
cards.back: Using a motor vehicle to commit a felony or causing a person’s death in a vehicle crash can lead to license loss.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about grounds for license loss, beginning with “Accumulating too many driving-record points under the”.
cards.back: Accumulating too many driving-record points under the applicable point system can cause license loss.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about grounds for license loss, beginning with “Failing to keep insurance proof for every owned vehicle”.
cards.back: Failing to keep insurance proof for every owned vehicle or driving a vehicle without insurance proof can lead to license loss.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about grounds for license loss, beginning with “A traffic-violation conviction for conduct before age sixteen can”.
cards.back: A traffic-violation conviction for conduct before age sixteen can cause license loss for an instruction-permit or restricted-permit holder.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about grounds for license loss, beginning with “Not paying a fine imposed for”.
cards.back: Not paying a fine imposed for a traffic-violation conviction can cause license loss.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about grounds for license loss, beginning with “Owing a South Dakota government agency at least one”.
cards.back: Owing a South Dakota government agency at least one thousand dollars is a listed basis for license loss.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about grounds for license loss, beginning with “A driver younger than eighteen can lose driving”.
cards.back: A driver younger than eighteen can lose driving privileges after a conviction for violating the license restrictions.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about grounds for license loss, beginning with “The handbook lists arrest for a blood-alcohol concentration from”.
cards.back: The handbook lists arrest for a blood-alcohol concentration from zero point zero two percent through zero point zero seven nine percent under SDCL thirty-two-twenty-three-twenty-one as a license-loss ground for a person under twenty-one.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about grounds for license loss, beginning with “Selling or distributing alcohol to someone”.
cards.back: Selling or distributing alcohol to someone younger than twenty-one can cause license loss.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about grounds for license loss, beginning with “Possessing alcohol while under twenty-one can”.
cards.back: Possessing alcohol while under twenty-one can be a ground for license loss.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about grounds for license loss, beginning with “Eluding law enforcement is a listed”.
cards.back: Eluding law enforcement is a listed ground for losing the driver license.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about revocation and reinstatement, beginning with “Revocation removes the driver license or the”.
cards.back: Revocation removes the driver license or the privilege to drive or apply for a license.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about revocation and reinstatement, beginning with “After revocation, the handbook requires the applicable tests, an”.
cards.back: After revocation, the handbook requires the applicable tests, an application fee and a reinstatement fee in its stated fifty dollars to two hundred twenty-five dollars range.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about revocation and reinstatement, beginning with “The reinstatement discussion specifically requires”.
cards.back: The reinstatement discussion specifically requires vision and knowledge tests following revocation.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about revocation and reinstatement, beginning with “The printed in-person reinstatement schedule lists DWI fees of”.
cards.back: The printed in-person reinstatement schedule lists DWI fees of one hundred dollars for a first offense, one hundred fifty dollars for a second and two hundred dollars for a third or later offense.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about revocation and reinstatement, beginning with “The printed in-person reinstatement schedule lists one hundred twenty-five”.
cards.back: The printed in-person reinstatement schedule lists one hundred twenty-five dollars for a second reckless-driving conviction within one year or for eluding an officer, two hundred twenty-five dollars for vehicular battery or homicide, and seventy-five dollars for other revocations.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about revocation and reinstatement, beginning with “Suspension removes the driver license or the”.
cards.back: Suspension removes the driver license or the privilege to drive or apply for a license.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about revocation and reinstatement, beginning with “After suspension, testing is unnecessary unless the license has”.
cards.back: After suspension, testing is unnecessary unless the license has expired, but the handbook requires an application fee and a fifty dollars reinstatement fee.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about minor sanctions and fees, beginning with “The first minor-sanction paragraph assigns thirty days of suspension,”.
cards.back: The first minor-sanction paragraph assigns thirty days of suspension, or another period required by law, when DPS receives a traffic-violation or credential-restriction conviction record for a minor under sixteen.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about minor sanctions and fees, beginning with “The next minor-permit paragraph assigns suspension for one hundred”.
cards.back: The next minor-permit paragraph assigns suspension for one hundred eighty days or until the sixteenth birthday, whichever is longer, after a second traffic-violation conviction, a restricted-permit violation, or a felony or Class one misdemeanor while on an instruction or restricted minor permit.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about minor sanctions and fees, beginning with “The minor-sanction section says receiving a felony or Class”.
cards.back: The minor-sanction section says receiving a felony or Class one misdemeanor conviction produces a suspension lasting one hundred eighty days or until the sixteenth birthday, whichever is longer, or another period required by law.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about minor sanctions and fees, beginning with “Reapplying after a felony or Class one misdemeanor suspension”.
cards.back: Reapplying after a felony or Class one misdemeanor suspension in the minor-sanction section requires a fifty dollars reinstatement fee and the license fee.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about minor sanctions and fees, beginning with “An unlicensed person under eighteen who receives a violation”.
cards.back: An unlicensed person under eighteen who receives a violation is subject to the corresponding minor suspension described in the handbook.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about minor sanctions and fees, beginning with “For an unlicensed minor, a second traffic offense, second”.
cards.back: For an unlicensed minor, a second traffic offense, second restricted-minor-permit violation, felony or Class one misdemeanor leads to the handbook’s longer period of one hundred eighty days or the time until the sixteenth birthday.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about minor sanctions and fees, beginning with “For a learner or restricted permit suspended after a”.
cards.back: For a learner or restricted permit suspended after a first traffic conviction or restriction violation, the fifty dollars reinstatement and application fees are waived unless a moving-offense conviction carries at least six points.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about minor sanctions and fees, beginning with “A learner or restricted permit holder in the”.
cards.back: A learner or restricted permit holder in the first-conviction suspension category may apply for a duplicate license.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about registration and title, beginning with “South Dakota residents must register vehicles and trailers they”.
cards.back: South Dakota residents must register vehicles and trailers they own and operate on public highways with the county treasurer for their home county.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about registration and title, beginning with “A vehicle brought from another state”.
cards.back: A vehicle brought from another state must be registered within ninety days.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about registration and title, beginning with “Registration renewal is staggered according to the”.
cards.back: Registration renewal is staggered according to the first letter of the owner’s last name.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about registration and title, beginning with “The renewal table assigns January to last names starting”.
cards.back: The renewal table assigns January to last names starting with A or B, February to C, D or E, and March to F, G or J.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about registration and title, beginning with “The renewal table assigns May to last names starting”.
cards.back: The renewal table assigns May to last names starting with H, I or O, June to K or L, and July to M or N.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about registration and title, beginning with “The renewal table assigns August to P, Q or”.
cards.back: The renewal table assigns August to P, Q or R, September to S, and November to T, U, V, W, X, Y or Z.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about registration and title, beginning with “Selling or transferring a vehicle”.
cards.back: Selling or transferring a vehicle requires its certificate of title.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about registration and title, beginning with “A vehicle title should be”.
cards.back: A vehicle title should be stored securely outside the vehicle.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about registration and title, beginning with “The vehicle’s registration certificate must be”.
cards.back: The vehicle’s registration certificate must be carried in the vehicle at all times.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about financial responsibility, beginning with “Before driving or reregistering a vehicle, future financial-responsibility proof”.
cards.back: Before driving or reregistering a vehicle, future financial-responsibility proof is required after license suspension or revocation tied to an uninsured-crash judgment, no-insurance conviction, vehicular homicide, DWI, or two reckless-driving convictions within one year.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about financial responsibility, beginning with “Most motorists establish future financial responsibility by asking their”.
cards.back: Most motorists establish future financial responsibility by asking their auto insurer to file an SR22 with the Driver Licensing Program.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about financial responsibility, beginning with “An SR22 must be sent directly by the insurer”.
cards.back: An SR22 must be sent directly by the insurer to the central administrative office, because exam stations cannot accept it.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about financial responsibility, beginning with “An owner of a vehicle that must be registered”.
cards.back: An owner of a vehicle that must be registered must continuously maintain a permitted form of financial responsibility.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about financial responsibility, beginning with “The handbook’s allowed financial-responsibility forms include an”.
cards.back: The handbook’s allowed financial-responsibility forms include an owner’s liability policy or a surety-company bond.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about financial responsibility, beginning with “Another financial-responsibility option is a certificate of deposit or”.
cards.back: Another financial-responsibility option is a certificate of deposit or securities worth fifty thousand dollars placed with the state treasurer.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about financial responsibility, beginning with “The handbook’s self-insurance-certificate option requires”.
cards.back: The handbook’s self-insurance-certificate option requires a minimum of twenty-six vehicles.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about financial responsibility, beginning with “Written financial-responsibility evidence must stay in the covered vehicle”.
cards.back: Written financial-responsibility evidence must stay in the covered vehicle and be shown to a law-enforcement officer on request.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about financial responsibility, beginning with “Acceptable insurance evidence includes a policy or identification card”.
cards.back: Acceptable insurance evidence includes a policy or identification card showing the insurer, policy number and coverage start and expiration dates.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about financial responsibility, beginning with “A state-treasurer certificate of deposit or a”.
cards.back: A state-treasurer certificate of deposit or a self-insurance certificate also qualifies as written financial-responsibility evidence.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about financial responsibility, beginning with “The handbook classifies a conviction for failing to maintain”.
cards.back: The handbook classifies a conviction for failing to maintain financial-responsibility proof as a Class two misdemeanor carrying thirty days in county jail, a one hundred dollars fine, or both.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about financial responsibility, beginning with “A conviction for failing to maintain financial-responsibility proof also”.
cards.back: A conviction for failing to maintain financial-responsibility proof also brings a license suspension of at least thirty days and at most one year.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about financial responsibility, beginning with “After the financial-responsibility violation described by the handbook, SR22”.
cards.back: After the financial-responsibility violation described by the handbook, SR22 insurance proof must be filed for three years measured from the eligibility date.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about financial responsibility, beginning with “Failure to file the required insurance proof causes suspension”.
cards.back: Failure to file the required insurance proof causes suspension of vehicle registration, license plates and the driver license.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about points and suspensions, beginning with “The point system subjects a driver to suspension for”.
cards.back: The point system subjects a driver to suspension for accumulating fifteen points within twelve consecutive months or twenty-two points within twenty-four consecutive months.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about points and suspensions, beginning with “When several offenses come from a single incident, points”.
cards.back: When several offenses come from a single incident, points are assigned for the offense with the highest point value.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about points and suspensions, beginning with “The point system assigns no points for speeding, standing,”.
cards.back: The point system assigns no points for speeding, standing, parking, equipment, size or weight violations, including damage-control speed limits set by the transportation department.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about points and suspensions, beginning with “Out-of-state convictions receive points in the same”.
cards.back: Out-of-state convictions receive points in the same way as convictions for conduct in South Dakota.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about points and suspensions, beginning with “A driver who requests a”.
cards.back: A driver who requests a hearing receives one before point-system suspension.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about points and suspensions, beginning with “The point-system suspension periods are sixty days for the”.
cards.back: The point-system suspension periods are sixty days for the first suspension, six months for the second and one year for later suspensions.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about points and suspensions, beginning with “The points table assigns ten points for DWI or”.
cards.back: The points table assigns ten points for DWI or DUI and also notes mandatory license revocation for intoxicated-driving convictions.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about points and suspensions, beginning with “Reckless driving carries eight points, while eluding or attempting”.
cards.back: Reckless driving carries eight points, while eluding or attempting to elude and drag racing each carry six points in the handbook’s table.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about points and suspensions, beginning with “Failure to yield, improper passing and driving on the”.
cards.back: Failure to yield, improper passing and driving on the wrong side each carry four points in the handbook’s table.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about points and suspensions, beginning with “A stop-sign or traffic-light violation carries three points, and”.
cards.back: A stop-sign or traffic-light violation carries three points, and another moving violation carries two points in the handbook’s table.
